output.review_comment:
The logic is basically right. Traced by hand, it should pass every test: mixed-case words like "NASA" and "iPhone" are kept as written (including at the start), "in," stays lowercase mid-title, small words are capitalised when first or last ("For", "The"), and the colon cases come out right ("Tricks: Best", "Field: A").

The blocking issue: to satisfy `test_subtitle_after_colon`, the PR adds a new rule (a small word right after a word ending in ':' gets capitalised). The docstring still says small words are lowercased "unless it is the first or the last word of `text`". So the function now does something its documentation says it won't, e.g. for "field: a year". The tests and docstring disagreed from the start. Treating the tests as the spec is right, since the teammate said they're the agreed spec, but the PR should make that explicit.

Please:
1. Update Rule 2 in the docstring to add the colon case, e.g. "...unless it is the first or last word of `text`, or directly follows a word ending in ':', in which case its first character is uppercased."
2. Add a PR description noting that the tests and docstring conflicted on the colon case and the tests were treated as the source of truth, so the editorial team can confirm it.

Minor: in `is_after_colon`, the `index > 0` check is redundant because `result` is only non-empty after the first word.
